City Council Meeting
MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
City Council, Community Development Financing Authority, Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*
March 19, 2012
A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor Ury at 05:06 p.m. , on March 19, 2012, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.
A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted by 5:00 p.m. on March 14, 2012, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the Norman P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.
*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."
Present:
Council Member Kelley
Council Member Leckness
Council Member Schlicht
Mayor Pro Tem Reardon
Mayor Ury
Absent:
None
Staff Present:
Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager
William P Curley III, City Attorney
Karen Hamman, City Clerk
PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Leckness
INVOCATION: Council Member Kelley
RECESS AND RECONVENE
At the hour of 5:08 p.m., Mayor Ury declared a recess. The City Council reconvened at 6:01 p.m. with all five City Council Members present.
PRESENTATIONS
P1.
Recognize Ruth Dicks on her 90th Birthday and 17 Years of Nursing Service at the Norman P. Community and Senior Center
Mayor Ury and Anna T. Boyce presented a Certificate of Appreciation to Ruth Dicks.
P2.
Recognize City Volunteers, for Their 1,000 Hours of Service
Mayor Ury presented Certificates of Appreciation to (1) Flora Kipper, Barbara Marine and Pollyann Patterson for volunteer hours at the Norman P. Murray Community and Senior Center; (2) Dan Moncino, Vince MacLean, and Les Sykes for volunteer hours with the Senior Community Activity Team (SCAT); and (4) JoAnn Hayden, Bari Russell, and Randy Smith for volunteer hours with the Mission Viejo Library. Additional volunteers, who were unable to attend the meeting, will receive their certificates at a later date.
P3.
Recognize Senior Citizens Activities Committee Member Elizabeth Busick for being chosen by UC Berkley’s School of Public Health as one of 30 exceptional Senior Volunteers in the State
Mayor Ury presented a Certificate of Commendation to Elizabeth Busick.
PUBLIC COMMENTS
Ross Chun and Lynn Hatton: extended an invitation to the 2012 Sustainability Forum on April 12, 2012, at 8:30 a.m. at Soka University in Aliso Viejo. Ms. Hatton discussed CUSD’s efforts to educate students through its Science, Technology, Engineering, Arts and Mathematics Initiative (STEAM) at Newhart Middle School and she invited the Council to an Earth Day Fair at Newhart on April 20, 2012, beginning at 5:00 p.m. Dan Avery, M.V.: thanked Mayor Pro Tem Reardon for bringing flowers to his home after his father-in-law passed away.
Wendy Bucknum, M.V.: announced a new class at Montanoso Recreation Center called RIPPED and she encouraged residents to visit the City’s web site for more information on this program as well as other classes at the recreation centers. She also discussed the Character Committee’s Chili cook-off and she thanked Mayor Pro Tem Reardon for judging. Mrs. Bucknum reminded residents of the Neighborhood Watch program and she encouraged residents to sign up or start a program in their neighborhood. She concluded by presenting a Certificate of Appreciation to Council Member Kelley, on behalf of the County of Orange, for her efforts with the Saddleback College Veterans Memorial.
CONSENT CALENDAR
Items 6 and 9 were removed from the Consent Calendar for separate discussion.
Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Council Member Leckness, to approve the Consent Calendar as described below.
On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:
AYES:
Council Member Kelley, Council Member Leckness, Council Member Schlicht, Mayor Pro Tem Reardon, and Mayor Ury
NOES:
None
ABSENT:
None
1.
Waive Reading of Ordinances and Resolutions
Approved the reading by title of all ordinances and resolutions and declared that said titles which appear on the public agenda shall be determined to have been read by title and further reading waived.
2.
City Council Minutes
Approved the Minutes for the regular City Council Meeting of March 5, 2012, as presented.
3.
Investment Policy Revisions
(1) Adopted Resolution 12-14 Revising the City Fiscal Year 2011-12 Investment Policy; and (2) adopted CDFA Resolution 12-01 Revising the Mission Viejo Community Development Financing Authority (MVCDFA) Fiscal Year 2011-12 Investment Policy.
4.
Check Register dated February 24, 2012 in the amount of $1,411,365.69
Ratified the accompanying check register.
5.
Check Register dated March 2, 2012 in the amount of $656,539.18
Ratified the accompanying check register.
7.
Community Development Agency (CDA) Treasurerâ??s Monthly Report for January 2012
Received and filed.
8.
Mission Viejo Community Development Financing Authority (MVCDFA) Treasurerâ??s Monthly Report for January 2012
Received and filed.
10.
Purchase of One Replacement Animal Services Vehicle
Awarded a purchase agreement for one Animal Services vehicle to Huntington Beach Ford in an amount not to exceed $60,220.85.
11.
Establish a Policy for "Deaf Child Near" Signs
Adopted Resolution 12-15 Establishing a Policy for the Installation of "Deaf Child Near" Signs.
PUBLIC HEARINGS
OLD BUSINESS
12.
Approve the Deeds for the Dog Park Land Swap with the County of Orange for the Mission Viejo Dog Park
Council Member Kelley announced that she would recuse herself from discussion of this item because she is a Board Member on the Orange County Parks Commission. City Attorney Curley reiterated his recommendation that Council Member Kelley not participate.
Council Member Kelley left the room at 6:38 p.m.
Dan Avery, M.V.: expressed his support for the proposed Dog Park.
The following presented written statements in favor of a dog park: Dorrie Steele, M.V. and Irma Kopstein, M.V.
The following presented a written statement in opposition to a dog park at City expense: Harry Lenczyk, M.V.
Motion made by Council Member Leckness, seconded by Mayor Ury, to authorize the City Manager, subject to any minor revisions required by the city attorney or city engineer, to (1) sign the Quit Claim Deed for the land swap of 2.71 acres of County park land to the City of Mission Viejo; (2) sign the Quit Claim Deed for the land swap of 7.18 acres of City land to the County of Orange for the Arroyo Trabuco trail connection; and( 3) sign the Easement Deed for 1.54 acres of City land for County trail access.
On roll call, said motion failed by the following vote:
AYES:
Council Member Leckness, and Mayor Ury.
NOES:
Council Member Schlicht, and Mayor Pro Tem Reardon.
ABSENT:
Council Member Kelley.
NEW BUSINESS
13.
Mid-Year Budget Review for FY 2011/12
City Manager Wilberg noted that this is the first mid-year report in roughly 4 years that shows a surplus without the need to make additional cuts.
Director of Administrative Services Cheryl Dyas presented the staff report.
Motion made by , seconded by , to
On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:
AYES:
Council Member Kelley, Council Member Leckness, Council Member Schlicht, Mayor Pro Tem Reardon, and Mayor Ury
NOES:
None
ABSENT:
None
ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR
6.
City Treasurer’s Monthly Report for January 2012
Council Member Schlicht drew the public’s attention to the balance of the City’s Investment portfolio which is $29.9 million as of January 31, 2012.
Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor Ury, to receive and file.
On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:
AYES:
Council Member Kelley, Council Member Leckness, Council Member Schlicht, Mayor Pro Tem Reardon, and Mayor Ury
NOES:
None
ABSENT:
None
9.
Mission Viejo Housing Authority (MVHA) Treasurer’s Monthly Report for January 2012
Director of Administrative Services Cheryl Dyas presented the staff report.
Council Member Schlicht expressed concern that Watermarke park fees would be disbursed before the State confirms that it approves of the Watermarke deal.
City Manager Wilberg noted that the Successor Agency Oversight Board must review the transaction before the matter is directed to the State. He further noted that the Watermarke park fees will not be spent for three years, until the statute of limitations expires.
Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Reardon, to receive and file.
On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:
AYES:
Council Member Kelley, Council Member Leckness, Council Member Schlicht, Mayor Pro Tem Reardon, and Mayor Ury
NOES:
None
ABSENT:
None
MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, AND COMMITTEE REPORTS
14.
Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Report
Stephen Wontrobski, M.V.: expressed concern with the Orange County Employees Retirement System (OCERS) investment returns and discussed the potential effect on OCFA employees.
Council Member Kelley presented the report.
15.
Foothill/Eastern Transportation Corridor Agency Report
Mayor Ury presented the report.
16.
San Joaquin Hills Transportation Corridor Agency Report
Mayor Pro Tem Reardon presented the report.
STAFF REPORTS
City Manager’s Report
City Manager Wilberg noted that staff will provide information relating to the City’s housing requirements at the next Council Meeting. The information will be part of the agenda and he hopes to clear up some current misconceptions about the City’s requirement to provide affordable housing.
City Attorney’s Report
City Attorney Curley noted that the FPPC has ruled that Council Members can vote on their appointment to regional boards as long as the City posts a notice on its web site to inform the public what stipend the Council Members receive on the outside boards and commissions.
Mr. Curley provided an overview of housing and the state's requirements relevant to low-income housing.
At the hour of 8:24 p.m., Mayor Ury vacated the dais. Mayor Ury returned at 8:25 p.m.
COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS
17.
Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended
The City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public record.
Council Member Kelley
Council Member Kelley recognized the volunteers that were honored at the beginning of the meeting. She stated that volunteers are the lifeblood of Mission Viejo and she thanked them for all that they do. She encouraged those who are interested in volunteering to contact the City and she noted that there are numerous opportunities in a variety of capacities. Council Member Kelley announced that there will be a blood drive in the Saddleback Room at City Hall on Wednesday, April 4, 2012, from 12:30 to 6:30 p.m. and she encouraged residents to put it on their calendars. She also announced that Olympic Gold Medalist and author Kristi Yamaguchi will visit Mission Viejo for the second time on March 20 to present her new children’s book. Council Member Kelley thanked Stephanie Tanton and the library staff for recruiting such notable authors for the City’s programs. She also outlined her visit with Philian Weygan Allan, a Council Member from Baguio City, Republic of the Philippines. Mrs. Allan came to Mission Viejo to learn about the City’s Community of Character Program and she was extremely impressed with the great things we do here. Council Member Kelley announced that she and Council Member Leckness met with Capistrano Unified School District ad hoc committee members earlier in the day. It was a productive meeting and she will provide a more in-depth report at the next City Council Meeting.
Council Member Leckness
Council Member Leckness discussed his attendance at Lord of the Strings concert with Laurence Juber last Saturday evening. Juber is a two-time Grammy winner and most famous for playing lead guitar in Paul McCartney’s Wings. Council Member Leckness stated that residents are very lucky to have the opportunity to hear such talented musicians here in Mission Viejo and he encouraged residents to attend the concerts. The next Lord of the Strings event will be held on Saturday, March 31, 2012, in the City Council Chamber.
Council Member Schlicht
Council Member Schlicht asked the City Attorney if documents become the Mission Viejo’s public records if a Council Member sits on a committee outside of the City. Mr. Curley replied that those documents are generally the public records of the other agency. Council Member Schlicht reminded her colleagues that Sharon Cody lobbied to remove the Animal Services Center as a potential dog park site and Mayor Ury lobbied against the Alicia Park location. She stated that she is not opposed to a dog park but she is opposed to a $1 million dog park. She has been an advocate for rotating a dog park in the City’s various parks and she visited dog parks in other cities while doing her research. She stated that there is opportunity to do something here but not for $1 million. Council Member Schlicht wished everyone a happy spring and she concluded with a quote from Federalist No. 62: “No government, any more than an individual, will long be respected without being truly respectable.”
Mayor Pro Tem Reardon
Mayor Pro Tem Reardon announced that the City has a program called Access MV where residents can report problems, ask questions, and communicate with the City. Access MV can be found on the right side of the City’s web site and she reminded residents of the great tool that is available to them. Mayor Pro Tem Reardon outlined her recent tour of Mission Viejo with staff members Randy Van Cott and Rich Schlesinger. She learned a lot about streets, slurry sealing and asphalt overlays and she thanked Director Chagnon for allowing his staff to spend so much time with her on the tour. She also attended the Chili Cook-Off that was mentioned earlier and she was very impressed with the young people who are involved in the Community of Character program. Mayor Pro Tem Reardon recognized several department heads for their thoughtful and purposeful problem-solving. She also thanked City Manager Wilberg for leading and supporting his staff to make intelligent choices in lowering the number of people that are working for the City. Mayor Pro Tem Reardon recommended that residents visit the web site www.sanonofresafety.org to learn more about the effort to get an initiative on the ballot so people can vote for or against the closure of San Onofre. She noted that she is a proponent of nuclear power as long as it’s safe but there appear to be a number of safety issues at San Onofre. Mayor Pro Tem Reardon reminded residents to pray for young cancer and stroke survivor, Cade Spinello. She noted that he is doing very well and she hopes he’ll be able to come to City Hall for a visit soon.
Mayor Ury
Mayor Ury announced that the Chamber of Commerce is holding its annual breakfast on Thursday, March 29, 2012, at 7:30 a.m. at the Mission Viejo Country Club and he concluded the meeting with a quote from Winston Churchill: "The pessimist looks at opportunity and only sees the difficulties, but the optimist looks at the difficulties and only sees opportunities."
ADJOURNMENT
At the hour of 8:51 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session, Mayor Ury adjourned the meeting to Monday, April 2, 2012, at 5:00 p.m.
______________________________________________
Karen Hamman, City Clerk
Approved at the meeting of April 02, 2012
